diagnosis:
I calibrated the model with DDS against NSE over 1971–1997 (4,500 runs) and submitted that model. Daily NSE is 0.81, KGE is 0.79 and r is 0.91. Simulated volume is about 11% above observed. The overestimate is mostly in 1971–84, a period with about 7% of discharge missing; in 1985–97 the bias is about 6%.

In a split-sample test, parameters calibrated on 1971–84 gave NSE 0.846 on 1985–97. The full-period parameters reach 0.859 there, but that is in-sample, not an independent check. Recalibrating on 1985–97 only raised it to 0.863. These results suggest the parameters transfer reasonably well over time, so I expect NSE of roughly 0.80–0.86 in 1998–2008.

Parameters:
- Soil: FC is about 215 mm, LP 0.49 and BETA 1.5.
- Response: fast quickflow (K1 about 0.36, MAXBAS about 2.9 days) and a moderate baseflow store (K2 about 0.076, PERC 1.8).

Snow parameters (TT, CFMAX, SFCF, CFR, CWH) are poorly identified because snow is only about 1.6% of precipitation. A low SFCF (0.69) probably makes up for volume errors rather than reflecting real snow processes. K0 and UZL changed a lot between calibrations with almost no change in NSE, so the threshold for fast surface runoff is also poorly identified.

Weaknesses: the model tends to overestimate total volume and probably low flows in summer droughts. Urban runoff, the reservoir and possible abstractions are not represented. Calibrating on KGE removed the volume bias but lowered NSE to 0.78, so I kept the NSE-optimal set.
